e.etymology: In Hungarian, Aliz is the form of Alice, from Germanic Adalheid, of noble kind. In the US it can also be a clipped form of Alize or Aliza.
A modern American name that crosses Addison with the -ley of Hadley; Adley is also an English surname.
A Latin American pet-style form of Liana, itself a short form of names such as Juliana and Liliana.
A short form of Tucker, an English occupational surname for a fuller, who beat and cleaned woven cloth. Tuck is also a surname of its own.
e.note: Rhymes with a common swear word, an easy target for playground teasing.

e.etymology: A modern name that extends Zaya or Zayna with the -ana ending.
In American use, a Hawaiian-style girls' name close to Kailani and Kalani, ending in lani, the Hawaiian word for sky or heaven.
A Bulgarian name that grew out of Ana or Angelina, helped along by Aniela, the heroine of Henryk Sienkiewicz's novel Without Dogma. In the US it also reads as a twist on Amelia.
A modern American coinage in the Kamiyah and Amayah family.
A recent name that matches Greek xylon, wood, the root of xylophone. In sound it sits beside Zylan and Dylan.
A spelling of Aryan, from Sanskrit arya, noble or honorable, a common boys' name in India. Persian has a related name, Arian.
e.note: Sounds like Aryan, a word the Nazis took over for their racial ideology; some Americans react to it.

assoc.t: sounds like Aryan, the racial term of Nazism

e.etymology: A recent Latin American style name in the family of Aliana and Eliany.
The Spanish and Portuguese Bible spelling of Achsah, from a Hebrew word for an anklet. In the Book of Joshua she is the daughter of Caleb, who asks her father for springs of water.

e.meaning: son of Magge, a medieval form of Margaret
e.etymology: An English surname that began as a matronymic: the son of Magge, a medieval short form of Margaret. It has recently been taken up as a first name for its x.
A modern blend of Millie and Anna, close to Emiliana and Liliana.
The feminine of Lucilius, a Roman family name formed from Lucius, which goes back to Latin lux, light. Today it is mainly a Portuguese name.
A spelling of Macklin, a Scottish and Irish surname taken up as a first name, often for the nickname Mack.

e.meaning: from the land of the lochs
e.etymology: A phonetic spelling of Lachlan, from Scottish Gaelic Lochlann, land of the lochs, the Gaels' name for Norway and so a byname for a Viking settler.
A recent name that gives Amara the opening of Emma and Emery.

e.meaning: first letter of the Hebrew alphabet
e.etymology: The name of the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, which began as a drawing of an ox's head. Actress Natalie Portman gave it to her son in 2011.
A Japanese girls' name written with many character combinations; common ones pair asa, morning or hemp, with mi, beauty. Asami Sato of The Legend of Korra introduced it to many Americans.

assoc.t: Asami Sato of The Legend of Korra

e.etymology: A recent coinage that adds the -ton of Paxton and Jaxton to Knox, a Scottish surname from Gaelic cnoc, hillock.

e.meaning: phoenix, the firebird reborn from its ashes
e.etymology: A respelling of Phoenix, the bird of Greek myth that burns and rises again from its ashes, from Greek phoinix, which also meant deep red. It is the name of Arizona's capital too.
A pet form of Noelle, the feminine of French Noel, Christmas, which goes back to Latin natalis, birth. Noelle is traditionally given to girls born near Christmas.
A recent boys' coinage that follows Messiah and Josiah in sound. It resembles Keziah, a daughter of Job in the Bible, but that name is feminine.
A K- spelling of Conan, an Irish name from cu, hound or wolf, with a diminutive ending; Konan is also the Breton form. The same spelling is a traditional name among the Baoule of Ivory Coast.
From Hebrew zakkai, pure or innocent. Zaccai is a family name in the books of Ezra and Nehemiah, and Yochanan ben Zakkai was a leading rabbi of the first century.
A recent blend of the Hux- of Huxley with the -son of Hudson and Jaxson.
An old Italian name from Eurus, the east wind of Greek myth. For most Americans it is the word for Europe's currency, which puts it beside recent wealth-themed names like Cash.

assoc.t: the euro, currency of the European Union

e.etymology: From an English surname for someone who lived by an enclosed yard, from Old Norse garthr. It is also used as a short form of the Welsh name Gareth.
namesakes: Garth Algar (Dana Carvey's character in Wayne's World)

e.etymology: From the gemstone, whose name comes through Old French grenat from Latin granatum, pomegranate, for its seed-like red crystals. It was a jewel name of the early 1900s for both sexes.

assoc.t: garnet, the deep red gem and January birthstone
Garnet, a Crystal Gem in Steven Universe

e.etymology: One of the modern spellings of Alicia, the Latinized form of Alice, which came through Old French from Germanic Adalheid, of noble kind.
